title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1966-07-17
source: SBD > RTR @ 15 I.p.s. > PCM > D > SSSB

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear 1966 soundboard capture with rare early gems like In The Pines and Cardboard Cowboy, highlighted by Pigpen’s organ and a standout Jerry solo.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers astonishingly clean, well‑balanced sound that lets every instrument shine – from the bouncy keys and driving bass to Pigpen’s vibrant organ and one of Jerry Garcia’s finest solos. The show itself is prized for its rarity, featuring early versions of “In The Pines” and “Cardboard Cowboy,” and while a few listeners felt it lacked a bit of energy, the overall performance is regarded as an exciting snapshot of the Dead’s formative era.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high reviewer scores (average 4.75), strong praise for both audio fidelity and musical moments, with only minor comments about energy; ample detailed feedback supports a confident rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers repeatedly describe the sound as crystal‑clear, crisp, fully separable and full‑sounding, with strong bass and bouncy keys; no significant flaws reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑era set praised for its rarity and unique song choices; some listeners note a slight dip in overall energy but the performance maintains strong momentum thanks to Pigpen’s organ and lively instrumental interplay.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia delivers one of his finest solos (noted on “Standing”), though one reviewer wished for more of him.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is described as active, moving and driving the sound forward.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ shines with a classic West‑Coast tone; keyboards are called strong and bouncy.
